title: Neighbor notes: Positive proof strip
summary: Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order. Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.
descriptionMd:
Two adjacent gauge readings describe how the press changed between successive sheets. Ada prepares a clean proof strip for the front desk. Positive derived readings keep their places relative to one another.

Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order.

Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.

Implement neighborNotesPositiveProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Adjacent array positions. Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with adjacent array positions. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
Produce readings[i] - readings[i-1] for i from 1 onward, preserving that order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
